title: Observability proxy splitter for VPC batching and tenant-level isolation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build an ingress proxy component that splits observability traffic at the VPC perimeter into tenant-scoped batches and an isolated low-trust path for on-prem customers. The proxy must support HTTP/gRPC mTLS, dynamic batching for metrics/logs to reduce downstream load, sampled tracing hooks for high-cardinality traces, and clear tenant quarantine semantics when an identity or quota violation is detected.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts observability traffic over mTLS and routes to tenant-specific upstreams or a quarantined bucket based on identity and policy
Batching reduces downstream write QPS by >= 40% for high-cardinality tenants without increasing median ingest latency by more than 50ms
Tracing hooks expose sampled span headers and inject per-request tenant metadata for downstream aggregation in Jaeger/Tempo-compatible collectors
Integration tests exercising tenant quarantine and re-route paths exist and run in CI with deterministic fixtures
Operational playbook and dashboard tiles for the proxy are added to the Console (ingest rate, batch sizes, quarantine events, error budget burn)
Documentation and upgrade notes for Private/VPC customers are published to Confluence and included in the Private install manifests
tasks: Design API for proxy policy language (RBAC + quota triggers) - owner: Liam
Implement TLS termination and mutual auth with customer KMS certs - owner: Security Infra
Add dynamic batching logic with backpressure signals - owner: Backend
Implement sampled tracing header passthrough and span tagging - owner: Runtime
Create end-to-end integration test harness for on-prem lab - owner: QA
Write Console dashboard queries and expose proxy metrics - owner: Observability UX
Prepare migration/rollout plan with canary and fast-failover rules - owner: SRE

notes: This ticket aims to reduce operational cost for Dedicated by batching high-cardinality tenant telemetry and to provide a clear isolation path for regulated Private customers. Implementation must balance latency SLOs for live customer-facing traces vs. cost savings on logs/metrics. Consider adding a lightweight fast-path for low-latency traces (no batching) when a trace header indicates p99-sensitive requests.
